title: Finder
summary: An in-memory full-text search index for help-centre articles.

tasks.title: Edited articles still match old words
brief: After an editor rewrote the “password” article to be about email settings, searching for “password” still returns it. Articles that are re-saved often also creep up the rankings.
Find the cause and fix it. Re-adding an article should behave exactly as if it had been removed and added fresh.
done: Re-adding a document replaces its old words and counts.
Removing a document after re-adding it leaves nothing behind.

questions: Is re-adding the normal way articles are edited? (Yes, the CMS re-saves the whole text.)
Should ranking reflect only the latest text? (Yes.)
orient: README rule: “adding a document with an existing id replaces it”.
Two symptoms (stale matches and rising rank) both suggest old postings surviving a re-add.
trace: add() overwrites docs[id] but only ever adds to postings, so old words and counts stay.
remove() already knows how to clean postings for an id, so add can call it first.
wrapUp: Cause: add never removed the previous version’s postings.
Fix: call this.remove(id) at the start of add, reusing the existing clean-up code.
With more time: an update() that diffs word sets, if re-indexing large articles becomes slow.

tasks.title: Prefix search
brief: Users type partial words. Support a trailing * on a query term: “pay*” matches payment, payments and payouts. Terms without * still match whole words only.
Prefix and exact terms combine with the usual AND rule and ranking. Matching is case-insensitive.
done: A term ending in * matches every indexed word that starts with it.
Exact terms are unchanged, and the two mix with AND semantics.
Ranking still counts occurrences of every matched word.

questions: Only trailing *? (Yes; a * in the middle is out of scope.)
Does a bare * match everything? (No; it tokenises to nothing and is ignored.)
orient: tokenize() strips the * because it splits on non-alphanumerics, so the * has to be noticed before tokenising.
search() builds scores per term from one posting; a helper that merges the postings of every word with the prefix slots straight in.
trace: Split the raw query on whitespace, remember which raw terms end in *, then tokenise each one.
A linear scan of the posting keys is simple and fine for a help centre; noted it as a scaling limit.
wrapUp: Added prefix terms by marking them before tokenising and merging postings for matching words.
Trade-off: prefix lookups scan every indexed word. A sorted word list or trie would fix that at scale.
Noticed but not changed: stop words with a * (for example “the*”) are dropped like any other stop word.
